fullPassage: Try to spot odd mix-ups next time you're in the supermarket. Have you noticed that supermarkets often charge ten times as much for fresh chili peppers in a package as for loose fresh chilies? That's because the typical customer buys such small quantities that he doesn't think to check whether they cost four cents or forty. Randomly tripling the price of a vegetable is a favorite trick: customers who notice the markup just buy a different vegetable that week; customers who don't have self-targeted a whopping price rise. I once spotted a particularly inspired trick while on a search for potato chips. My favorite brand was available on the top shelf in salt and pepper flavor and on the bottom shelf, just a few feet away, in other flavors, all the same size. The top-shelf potato chips cost 25 percent more, and customers who reached for the top shelf demonstrated that they hadn't made a price-comparison between two near-identical products in near-identical locations. They were more interested in snacking. Admittedly, for some people the difference in flavors is important. Some will notice the higher price for salt and pepper flavor and, irritated, pay anyway. Others will prefer the different flavors and count themselves lucky that they have inexpensive tastes. But this is an example of a universal truth about supermarkets: they are full of close (or not so close) substitutes, some cheap, some expensive, and with a strong random element to the pricing. The random element is there so that only shoppers who are careful to notice, remember, and compare prices will get the best bargains. If you want to outwit the supermarkets, simple observation is your best weapon. And if you can't be bothered to do that, you really don't need to save money.

(A) Randomly tripling the price of a vegetable is a favorite trick: customers who notice the markup just buy a different vegetable that week; customers who don't have self-targeted a whopping price rise.

(B) That's because the typical customer buys such small quantities that he doesn't think to check whether they cost four cents or forty.

(C) Have you noticed that supermarkets often charge ten times as much for fresh chili peppers in a package as for loose fresh chilies?

det.analysis:

questions.stem: 다음 주어진 문장이 들어갈 위치로 가장 적절한 곳은? [주어진 문장] They were more interested in snacking.

det.korean: 주어진 문장은 top-shelf 고객들이 가격 비교를 하지 않았다는 설명(demonstrated that they hadn't made a price-comparison) 바로 뒤, 'Admittedly(인정하건대)'로 시작하는 양보문 앞인 ③에 들어가야 자연스럽다. 가격 비교를 안 한 이유(간식에 더 관심 있었다)가 먼저 나오고, 그 다음 양보가 이어져야 한다.
det.analysis:
❌ ①: 칠리 고추 가격 질문 바로 뒤에는 그 이유(That's because~)가 바로 이어져야 하므로 '간식에 관심 있었다'는 문장이 들어갈 자리가 아니다.
❌ ②: 감자칩을 찾아다닌 트릭 소개 직후에는 선반 위치에 대한 구체적 설명이 이어져야 하므로 흐름상 적절하지 않다.
✅ ③: top-shelf 고객들이 가격 비교를 하지 않았다는 설명 바로 뒤에 '그들은 간식에 더 관심 있었다'는 이유가 이어지고, 그 다음 Admittedly로 양보가 이어지는 흐름이 가장 자연스럽다.
❌ ④: 이미 맛 선호에 대한 설명이 끝난 뒤이므로 '간식에 관심 있었다'는 문장이 뒤늦게 들어가면 흐름이 끊긴다.
det.tip: Admittedly처럼 양보를 나타내는 연결어 앞에는 반드시 양보할 대상이 되는 내용(앞선 주장)이 먼저 나와야 한다는 점을 확인하자.

det.korean: 만약 당신이 슈퍼마켓보다 한 수 앞서고 싶다면, 간단한 관찰이 최고의 무기이다.

det.tip: 글의 핵심 소재(슈퍼마켓 가격, 소비자 관찰)와 무관한 소재(산책, 취미 등)가 갑자기 등장하는 문장을 찾자.

questions.passage: Try to spot odd mix-ups next time you're in the supermarket. Have you noticed that supermarkets often charge ten times as much for fresh chili peppers in a package as for loose fresh chilies? That's because the typical customer buys such small quantities that he doesn't think to check whether they cost four cents or forty. Randomly tripling the price of a vegetable is a favorite trick: customers who notice the markup just buy a different vegetable that week; customers who don't have self-targeted a whopping price rise. I once spotted a particularly inspired trick while on a search for potato chips. My favorite brand was available on the top shelf in salt and pepper flavor and on the bottom shelf, just a few feet away, in other flavors, all the same size. The top-shelf potato chips cost 25 percent more, and customers who reached for the top shelf demonstrated that they hadn't made a price-comparison between two near-identical products in near-identical locations. They were more interested in snacking. Admittedly, for some people the difference in flavors is important. __________ Others will prefer the different flavors and count themselves lucky that they have inexpensive tastes. But this is an example of a universal truth about supermarkets: they are full of close (or not so close) substitutes, some cheap, some expensive, and with a strong random element to the pricing. The random element is there so that only shoppers who are careful to notice, remember, and compare prices will get the best bargains. If you want to outwit the supermarkets, simple observation is your best weapon. And if you can't be bothered to do that, you really don't need to save money.

우리말: 어떤 사람들은 소금과 후추 맛의 더 높은 가격을 알아차리고도 짜증나지만 어쨌든 지불한다.

questions.stem: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 단어를 어법에 맞게 영어로 한 단어로 쓰시오. (원형: demonstrate)

det.korean: 주어는 복수 customers이고 과거 시제 문맥(cost, reached)이므로 demonstrate의 과거형 demonstrated가 되어야 한다.
det.analysis: ✅ demonstrated: 앞뒤 문장이 모두 과거 시제(cost, reached)이므로 시제 일치를 위해 demonstrate의 과거형을 써야 한다.
det.tip: 문맥의 시제(과거 서술)에 동사 형태를 일치시키는 것이 어형변환의 핵심이다.

questions.passage: But this is an example of a universal truth about supermarkets: they are full of close (or not so close) substitutes, some cheap, some expensive, and with a strong random element to the pricing. The random element is there so that only shoppers who are __________ to notice, remember, and compare prices will get the best bargains.
questions.stem: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 단어를 어법에 맞게 영어로 한 단어로 쓰시오. (원형: care)

det.korean: 빈칸 뒤에 to notice, remember, compare 같은 행동을 묘사하는 형용사가 필요하므로 명사/동사 care에 형용사형 어미 -ful을 붙여 careful이 되어야 한다.
det.analysis: ✅ careful: who가 이끄는 관계사절의 보어 자리이므로 형용사 형태가 필요하다. 명사 care에 -ful을 붙여 '주의 깊은'이라는 의미의 형용사를 만든다.
det.tip: 관계사절 안에서 be동사(are) 뒤에는 형용사가 보어로 와야 한다는 점을 기억하자.
